## Publication identity

Published head: `b89e7047ea352a3d47703b134c6c12a7ea589a04`; complete tree: `1167b49fec0bcc95eac247111f684e786b628536`. The remote tree exactly matches local documentation commit `a09585fa67a458e76b303344d5756138a6e7234c`. Only 35 documentation paths follow the executed source; executable content is unchanged from `53aa9fe93c8599c41c0b9b2df4f438b969f14ce9`.

Concurrent [PR #70](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/CLASSifiedisRUPTed/pull/70) remains separate and unchanged at `eb9577bf9403741c53c2a53f6d5a67fd4e0825a9`; its PWA changes are not included here.

## Problem and change

The existing future-codec case checked rejection and an uninitialized identity, then successfully retried the same destination with a compatible registry. It did not directly observe persisted rows between rejection and retry.

This test-only follow-up reads all object-store keys and values in one read-only transaction on the existing destination database. The observer rejects unexpected creation or upgrade, closes its connection, and does not claim a writer fence.

The test requires an empty records baseline, an exactly unchanged complete snapshot immediately after rejection, and unchanged persisted payload after reopening. Only the documented `meta['writer']` replacement is excluded across the intentional reopen; encryption headers, inventory and every other row remain observable. The existing compatible retry must produce visible physical records, preventing an always-empty observation from passing.

All 25 original `expect(` starts and their matcher behavior remain, with four additions. The valid signed/encrypted backup, compatible controls, same destination, complete records, revisions/timestamps, principal, signatures and final encrypted reopen remain. The case limit is still **30,000 ms**. Production code, schemas, backup meaning, cryptography, dependencies, workflows and product caps are unchanged.

## Source-specific validation

Executed source: `53aa9fe93c8599c41c0b9b2df4f438b969f14ce9`; tree: `81a97a7be19975fe653bce41bda5d7e0991efcbb`.

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Targeted future-codec integration | 1 case passed in 1 file; no failed/pending entries; case 13.259 s, command 14.547 s |
| Full TypeScript | Passed |
| Specification, dependency and strict registry checks | Passed |
| Tooling | 27 passed; zero failed/cancelled/skipped/todo |
| CLI | 46 passed; zero failed/cancelled/skipped/todo |
| Non-interactive setup and production build | Passed |

Fresh code, functional and defensive source reviews found no blocking finding in this test-only delta. The observation covers persisted state after settled rejection in fake IndexedDB; it supplies no native interruption, quota or crash result.

The parent's full run remains **839 entries across 95 files: 832 passed, 3 failed, 4 pending**, with its timeout and reporter evidence retained. Its earlier focused pass and later isolated diagnostics remain separate. This selected pass does not replace that history, establish a timeout cause or qualify the full suite. The complete domain suite was not rerun locally for this follow-up.

## Relationship and remaining gate

This commit retains [PR #69](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/CLASSifiedisRUPTed/pull/69)'s published head `6d4f6ea7ba9bcf886ae69edd0f167a621308d4b2` as its parent and targets `main`, so hosted CI qualifies the complete proposed tree. The executable diff from #69 is only the future-codec integration test; all five #64–#68 histories remain ancestral. PR #69's branch stays unchanged.

The [follow-up cycle](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/CLASSifiedisRUPTed/tree/b89e7047ea352a3d47703b134c6c12a7ea589a04/docs/development/cycles/20261120-restore-rejection-proof) contains the handoff, three source reviews, independent evidence review and 28-member evidence archive. The original parent cycle and its unsuccessful results remain intact. All 51 historical readiness findings stay open.

**Draft pending actual current-head hosted qualification.** Inspect Alpha and CLI outcomes and their checked-out source before integration. No deployment or release is included.
